decks.name: LeetCode #23 - Merge k Sorted Lists
decks.description: Merge k sorted linked lists into one sorted linked list

cards.question: Merge k Sorted Lists: You are given an array of k linked-lists lists, each linked-list is sorted in ascending order. Merge all the linked-lists into one sorted linked-list and return it.

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.explanation: Extract all node values from all k lists into an array, sort the array, then rebuild a new linked list from sorted values. Simple approach but requires O(n) extra space for storing all values and O(n log n) sorting time. Not optimal but straightforward to implement.

solutions.name: Iteration
solutions.explanation: Repeatedly scan all k lists to find the minimum node, add it to result, and advance that list's pointer. Continue until all lists are exhausted. Simple but inefficient with O(n*k) time complexity since we scan all k lists for each of n nodes. Good for understanding but not optimal.

solutions.name: Merge Lists One By One
solutions.explanation: Sequentially merge lists by taking first two lists, merging them, then merging result with third list, and so on. Uses standard two-list merge algorithm repeatedly. Simple to implement but inefficient with O(n*k) time since early lists get traversed multiple times. Better than scanning all lists but still not optimal.

solutions.name: Heap
solutions.explanation: Use min heap to efficiently track minimum among k list heads. Initially push first node from each list into heap. Repeatedly pop minimum node, add to result, and push its next node into heap. Heap maintains k elements with O(log k) operations. Total O(n log k) time for n nodes. Optimal solution with clean implementation using priority queue.

solutions.name: Divide And Conquer (Recursion)
solutions.explanation: Use divide and conquer approach to merge lists in pairs recursively. Split k lists into two halves, recursively merge each half, then merge the two results. Forms binary tree of merges with log k depth. Each level processes all n nodes once. Total O(n log k) time. Elegant recursive solution with minimal space due to call stack only.
